zone.name: Lower Manhattan south of Chambers Street
zone.notes: MVP coverage only. Places north of Chambers, in Brooklyn, or not street-accessible are omitted.

places.name: Irish Hunger Memorial
places.one_liner: A County Mayo stone cottage and a quarter-acre of Irish hillside stacked above Vesey Street.

places.name: Woolworth Building
places.one_liner: The old Cathedral of Commerce still pins the skyline; the lobby is tour-only, the facade is free.

places.name: 5 Beekman Street
places.one_liner: Temple Court sat empty for decades; the nine-story iron atrium is now a hotel you can still gawk at from Beekman.

places.name: Barthman's Sidewalk Clock
places.one_liner: A working clock face set into the Broadway sidewalk at Maiden Lane. Look down.

places.name: Trinity Place Bank Vault Bar
places.one_liner: Cocktails inside a 1904 Mosler vault whose doors weigh 35 tons each, under 115 Broadway.

places.name: Trinity Churchyard
places.one_liner: Manhattan's oldest carved gravestone, a pigpen cipher, and Hamilton, boxed in by towers.

places.name: St. George's Syrian Catholic Church
places.one_liner: A boarded landmark on Washington Street, leftover from the Syrian colony razed for the Battery Tunnel.

places.name: Titanic Memorial Lighthouse
places.one_liner: Molly Brown pushed for this lighthouse; it now marks the Seaport instead of dropping a noon time ball.

places.name: Wall Street Palisade
places.one_liner: Wooden pavers in the cobbles trace the 1653 wall that named the street.

places.name: Wall Street Bombing Scars
places.one_liner: Pockmarks still pitted into 23 Wall Street from the 1920 wagon bomb that killed 38 people.

places.name: Site of New York Slave Market
places.one_liner: A small plaque near 74 Wall Street marks where the city ran a municipal slave market.

places.name: Standard Oil Building
places.one_liner: Rockefeller's old HQ bends with Broadway and still wears a pyramid meant to greet incoming ships.

places.name: Skyscraper Museum
places.one_liner: A 10-foot-high gallery at 39 Battery Place that makes Lower Manhattan's towers feel like models.

places.name: Wavertree
places.one_liner: An 1885 iron-hulled full-rigger parked at Pier 16, one of the last of her kind still afloat.

places.name: Delmonico's
places.one_liner: The Beaver Street original; two marble columns out front are rumored to have come from Pompeii.

places.name: Oldest Fence in New York
places.one_liner: The 1771 Bowling Green fence that once guarded a statue of King George — sawed-off crowns still show.

places.name: September 11th Garden Braemar Stone
places.one_liner: A river stone from near Balmoral sitting in the Queen Elizabeth II garden off Hanover Square.

places.name: 77 Water Street
places.one_liner: Street-level oddities plus a fake WWI biplane parked on the roof like it just landed.

places.name: Preserved Remnants of 17th Century New York
places.one_liner: Dutch Stadt Huys and Lovelace Tavern foundations under glass in the sidewalk at 85 Broad Street.

places.name: American Merchant Mariners' Memorial
places.one_liner: Bronze sailors on a sinking prow; the man in the water disappears under the tide twice a day.

places.name: The Elevated Acre
places.one_liner: A lawn and river view hiding up an escalator at 55 Water Street.

places.name: Fraunces Tavern
places.one_liner: Washington's farewell dinner site, still a tavern and a small museum at Pearl and Broad.

places.name: SeaGlass Carousel
places.one_liner: Glowing fish spinning inside a glass nautilus on the old New York Aquarium footprint.
